Dehydrate a 4 in. silicon wafer at 200 °C for 20 min, then apply an adhesion promoter for 30 s at 120 °C. Spin coat the wafer with SU-8 2050 (high contrast, epoxy-based) photoresist using a spread cycle of 70 and 22 × g for 30 s and a development cycle of 1,000 and 0.5 × g for 30 s in order to achieve a desired film thickness in the z-axis ( e.g. , 50 μm in this protocol). Conduct a cycle of edge bead removal for 30 s using edge bead removal solvent. Directly write the pattern to the SU-8 film using a dose of 365 nm UV light at 100 mJ/cm 2 . Crosslink the film pattern by baking on a hotplate and ramping the temperature at 5 °C/min, starting at 23 °C and holding at 90 °C to dry out the solvents. The ramping profile is achieved by proximity, plus vacuum contact bake steps, for a total duration of 805 s. Allow the film to cool on the hotplate to room temperature. Note: Keep the film on the hotplate to avoid thermal stress. Develop unexposed SU-8 photoresist using fresh developer solution for 3.5 min in a rocker. Rinse the wafer with IPA. Dry the wafer using pressurized nitrogen. Hard-bake the wafer at 150 °C for 30 min. Note: Alternatively, follow the Permanent Epoxy Negative Photoresist Processing Guidline from MicroChem. steps.title: Prepare all buffers and solutions
steps.instruction: Make 1× PBS (137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 10 mM Na₂HPO₄, 1.8 mM KH₂PO₄, pH 7.4) and store at room temperature up to 1 year; prepare 10 % Extran (40 mL Extran® MA 02 + 360 mL ddH₂O, pH 7.0) fresh before each use; make Blocking buffer (2 % BSA in 1× PBS, pH 7.4) aliquot and store at –20 °C (avoid >2 freeze‑thaw cycles); prepare HEPES‑Tyrode’s buffer without glucose (20 mM HEPES, 134 mM NaCl, 0.34 mM Na₂HPO₄, 2.9 mM KCl, 12 mM NaHCO₃, 1 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM CaCl₂, pH 7.4) and store at room temperature up to 1 year, adding 5 mM D‑glucose fresh before use.

steps.title: Fabricate SU‑8 master on silicon wafer
steps.instruction: Dehydrate a 4‑inch P‑type silicon wafer at 200 °C for 20 min, then apply adhesion promoter for 30 s at 120 °C. Spin‑coat SU‑8 2050 using a spread cycle of 70 × g for 30 s then 22 × g for 30 s, followed by a development cycle of 1,000 × g for 30 s and 0.5 × g for 30 s to obtain ~50 µm thickness. Perform edge‑bead removal with edge‑bead remover solvent for 30 s. Expose the SU‑8 film to 365 nm UV light at 100 mJ cm⁻². Bake on a hot plate: ramp from 23 °C to 90 °C at 5 °C min⁻¹, hold at 90 °C for a total of 805 s (including proximity and vacuum contact bake). Cool to room temperature on the hot plate. Develop unexposed SU‑8 in fresh developer for 3.5 min on a rocker, rinse with IPA, dry with pressurised N₂, then hard‑bake at 150 °C for 30 min. Transfer the wafer, SU‑8 side up, into a 150 mm Petri dish and secure with Scotch tape.

steps.title: Cast and cure PDMS on the master
steps.instruction: Mix Sylgard 184 base and curing agent at a 10:1 weight ratio (e.g., 180 g base + 18 g agent for 198 g total); stir until no streaks are visible. Degas the mixture in a Nalgene® vacuum desiccator for 30 min (longer if >200 g; e.g., 2 h for 200 g in a 100 mm dish). Pour the PDMS over the mold to a thickness of 4–5 mm. Cure in an oven at 80 °C for 4 h. Cut the cured PDMS block (typical size 4 cm × 2 cm × 5 mm) from the wafer with linear cuts, avoiding damage to the mold. Using a 6 mm biopsy punch create an inlet well at one channel end and a 1 mm biopsy punch create the outlet at the opposite end.

steps.title: Clean PDMS biochip
steps.instruction: Place the biochip in 400 mL 10 % Extran and sonicate 15 min; blow‑dry with compressed air. Sonicate in 100 % Butan‑1‑ol for 30 min (PDMS will swell temporarily); blow‑dry. Sonicate again in 10 % Extran for 10 min; blow‑dry. Finally sonicate in dH₂O for 10 min; blow‑dry completely before further use.

steps.title: Bond PDMS to #1 coverslip
steps.instruction: Place the cleaned PDMS chip channel‑side down onto a #1 borosilicate coverslip; press gently with the palm and smooth any bubbles with a finger to obtain a tight seal. Ensure the coverslip is dust‑free (clean as described in the cleaning steps). Store the bonded chip in a sealed container away from light; it can be reused at least ten times provided it remains flat and unstretched.

steps.title: Coat channel with fibrinogen
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of fibrinogen (40 µg mL⁻¹ in PBS, pH 7.4) to the 6 mm inlet well. Using a 1.5 mL transfer pipette, draw the solution through the channel and out the 1 mm outlet, ensuring the channel is completely filled (no air bubbles). Incubate the chip for 2 h at 25 °C. Wash by drawing 100 µL Tyrode’s buffer (or PBS) through the channel with the same pipette technique. Add 100 µL blocking buffer, draw through the channel, and incubate 30 min at 25 °C. Wash again with 100 µL Tyrode’s/PBS and keep the buffer in the channel until imaging to prevent bubble formation.

steps.title: Isolate human platelets
steps.instruction: Collect 8 mL venous blood into an ACD tube. Centrifuge at 200 × g for 20 min (no brake); collect the platelet‑rich plasma (PRP) supernatant and let it rest in a 37 °C water bath for 30 min. Immediately add prostaglandin E1 to a final concentration of 1 µM, then centrifuge PRP at 800 × g for 20 min (no brake). Discard the platelet‑poor plasma, resuspend the pellet in HEPES‑Tyrode’s buffer with glucose. Perform a platelet count and adjust the concentration to 3 × 10⁵ µL⁻¹. Five minutes before perfusion, add calcein to a final concentration of 1 µg mL⁻¹, keep the suspension in the dark and use within 1 h (fluorescence is lost after that).

steps.title: Isolate mouse platelets (optional)
steps.instruction: Collect 1 mL mouse blood by cardiac puncture (post‑CO₂ euthanasia) or inferior vena cava venipuncture. Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min; collect PRP and the top 1/8 of the red‑cell layer. Add 200 µL HEPES‑Tyrode’s with glucose to the red‑cell fraction, mix, and centrifuge again at 400 × g for 5 min. Pool the supernatant with the previously collected PRP. Centrifuge the pooled PRP at 200 × g for 6 min; collect the supernatant without disturbing remaining cells, add 200 µL buffer to the red‑cell layer, mix, and centrifuge at 200 × g for 6 min; pool the supernatant again. Rest the pooled PRP 10 min at room temperature, add PGE1 to 0.5 µM, then centrifuge at 500 × g for 10 min. Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in HEPES‑Tyrode’s with glucose, count platelets and adjust to 3 × 10⁵ µL⁻¹. Incubate with anti‑GPIb‑488 antibody (3 µg mL⁻¹) for 10 min at room temperature in the dark.

steps.title: Assemble syringe‑pump flow system
steps.instruction: Connect a 2 mL glass Luer‑lock syringe to the horizontal female Luer lock on a 3‑way stopcock. Slip silicone tubing onto the male Luer lock and secure with the rotating lock. Attach a 20 mL plastic Luer‑lock syringe filled with water to the opposite female Luer lock (used for flushing). Mount the glass syringe on the PHD syringe pump and secure it. Bend a 30 mm length of 1 mm‑diameter steel tubing 90°, insert the opposite end into medical‑grade Tygon tubing, and place the metal tubing into the 1 mm outlet of the PDMS chip. Place the assembled chip on the microscope stage, bring the coverslip into focus, and verify a tight seal.

steps.title: Perform perfusion assay and imaging
steps.instruction: Empty the inlet well of the chip. Add 100 µL of the prepared platelet suspension (3 × 10⁵ µL⁻¹) to the inlet well. Start the syringe pump and draw fluid through the channel at 5 µL min⁻¹ (corresponding to a shear rate of 500 s⁻¹) for 5 min. Acquire a time‑stack of both DIC and fluorescence (excitation 488 nm, emission 520 nm) images at regular intervals. Keep Tyrode’s buffer or PBS in the channel after washing to avoid air bubbles during imaging. All perfusion steps are performed in the dark.

steps.title: Calculate flow rates for desired shear
steps.instruction: Use Q = W h² γ̇ × 10⁴ where Q is flow rate (µL min⁻¹), W is channel width (cm), h is channel height (cm), and γ̇ is desired shear rate (s⁻¹). Alternatively, calculate wall shear stress τ = 6 µ Q / (W h²) with µ the fluid viscosity (e.g., 0.71 × 10⁻³ Pa·s for washed platelets at 37 °C). Refer to the provided table for common shear rates and corresponding flow rates (e.g., 150 s⁻¹ → 1.5 µL min⁻¹, 500 s⁻¹ → 5 µL min⁻¹, 1000 s⁻¹ → 10 µL min⁻¹).

steps.title: Coat Vena8 Fluoro+ commercial chip
steps.instruction: Aspirate 10 µL of fibrinogen (40 µg mL⁻¹ in PBS, pH 7.4) or vWF (100 µg mL⁻¹ in PBS, pH 7.4) with a 20 µL pipette and place the tip into one channel opening; depress the plunger to fill the channel (the channel becomes transparent). Place the chip in a moist container (tissue wetted with dH₂O) and incubate overnight at 4 °C. Remove the coating solution, aspirate 10 µL blocking buffer, fill the channel and incubate 1 h at room temperature. Aspirate 10 µL PBS, fill the channel to wash; repeat the wash once. Connect tubing to the outlet pins, submerge the inlet tubing in an Eppendorf tube containing washed platelets, and connect the outlet tubing to a Mirus Evo Nanopump.

steps.title: Run Vena8 assay with software
steps.instruction: Power on the PC, lamp, motor controller, screen, stage controller, CCD camera, microscope, temperature controller, and Mirus Evo Nanopump. Launch VenaFlux Assay x64 software, create a new protocol, and execute the following commands in order (right‑click each): VenFlux Setup → Initialize platform → Start video preview → Geometry setup → Update geometry → Washout pump → Washout cable → Wash/connect biochip → Washout chip → Cell assay. For ‘Cell assay’, set shear units, acquisition time, and capture delay as required, then right‑click ‘Start assay’ to begin flow and data capture. To stop, click ‘Stop assay’. Use ‘Acquire image to file’ or ‘Acquire video to file’ to save data. Analyze images with ImageJ or ImagePro Premier.
